slides.say: n is an odd number. Which of the following is the most precise description of nine n squared minus one, over four?

So n is odd, and the whole top, nine n squared minus one, is divided by four. We need the most precise description of the result. We'll start with one allowed value and check the choices. Then [short pause] we'll use the difference-of-squares formula to settle any choices that are still possible.
[short pause] Let's start by plugging in. n has to be odd, so try n is one. Nine times one is nine, minus one is eight. Eight over four is two.
Our result is two, so check the choices now. Choice number two says odd or a non-integer fraction. Two is neither, so that choice is out.

Choice numbers one, three and four still allow an even result. But choice numbers three and four also allow a non-integer fraction, and choice number three allows an odd result too. Getting more even examples would not show that these other results are impossible. So we will not keep plugging in just to get the same kind of answer.
Instead, let's check whether the expression must always give an even integer. If it does, always even is the most precise description. We can decide that using the difference-of-squares formula.
at: always even is the most precise description

slides.say: [pause] Rewrite the top using the difference-of-squares formula. Nine n squared is the whole product, three n, squared. So nine n squared minus one is three n minus one, times three n plus one.
n is odd, so three n is odd too. Three n minus one and three n plus one are the even numbers just before and after it. They are even numbers in a row, and their product always divides by eight.
at: n is odd, so three n

slides.say: So the top is eight times an integer k. Eight k over four is two k, which is always even. Choice number one is our answer. Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
